comment:
Read at commit 8f15282 of celestebetancur/Chrysalis, the head of the repository. Three commits carry version 2.0.2 — e8ec031, 5b86287 and 8f15282 — and they differ only in the Windows cross-build: git diff over src/ and res/ between the first and the last is empty, so any of them describes the installed build.

The jacks get no family. What a Chrysalis input or output carries is decided entirely by the .ck program compiled into it, exactly as Host's audio jacks are decided by the hosted plugin, so no colour is the honest answer.

The outputs and the inputs are scaled differently and the maker knows it: line 177 of src/Chrysalis.cpp carries the comment "TODO: Check this values to make them correspond to VCV Rack". Inputs are divided by 5, so 5V is ChucK's 1.0; outputs are multiplied by 1.0, so ChucK's 1.0 is 1V. A signal sent straight through the module comes out at a fifth of the level it went in.

The two buttons and the two text labels are built with createWidget rather than createParam, so they are Widgets with no ParamQuantity, carry no paramPos, and cannot be reached by a help click. They take Note lines. The compile lamp is a LightWidget and is likewise not one of the three lists a click walks.

autoload.txt ships beside the plugin with the single word test.ck, and the constructor compiles it whenever a module is created without saved state, so the module is never truly idle on arrival. test.ck is installed alongside it and is the program described in the Note.

There is no manual: manualUrl in plugin.json is empty and the README covers only building and the four global floats. The knob names Knob 1 to Knob 4 and the jack names adc 1 to adc 4 and dac 1 to dac 4 are the only labels anywhere — the panel art prints none of them, only the module name, the ChucK logo and the maker's byline.

The module registers no context menu of its own: there is no appendContextMenu anywhere in the source, so the file is loaded from the panel buttons and nowhere else.
